narrative:
346 requests were captured across 122 unique URLs and 18 hosts. The traffic is dominated by read-only GET requests to Premier League APIs (api.premierleague.com and sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com) plus a significant amount of analytics and tracking noise (TikTok, Spotify pixels, Blaze audit, Adobe, Google adtrafficquality, Sentry, Firebase). Core high-interest data endpoints include: (1) Premier League content APIs under /content/premierleague for VIDEO, PLAYLIST, PROMO, TEXT and generic content listings; (2) match and competition data under sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com, including /api/v2/matches, /api/v5/competitions/8/seasons/{season}/standings, /api/v1/competitions/8/seasons/{season}/teams, /api/v1/matches/{matchId}/events, and /api/v3/matches/{matchId}/lineups; and (3) player and team data via /api/v1/players/{id}, /api/v2/competitions/8/seasons/{season}/players/{id}/stats, /api/v1/competitions/8/seasons/{season}/teams/{teamId}/form, nextfixture and leaderboards. These together provide the structured data needed to automate tasks such as retrieving fixtures, standings, team form, player stats, and related editorial/video content for clubs.

There are no login or user-specific auth flows in this capture; all core data endpoints appear to be publicly accessible, relying only on standard cookies and possibly generic app-level configuration (Firebase, Blaze SDK). Auth-related patterns observed are limited to: (a) API keys embedded as query parameters for Blaze SDK endpoints (api_key in the query string), (b) Firebase Installations and Remote Config endpoints which issue installation IDs and fetch remote config, and (c) Adobe Experience Cloud consent endpoints. No Bearer tokens, CSRF headers, or explicit X-API-Key headers were seen. Roughly a third of requests are noise: analytics pixels (TikTok, Spotify), Blaze event audit, Sentry, Adobe, Google adtrafficquality/SODAR, reCAPTCHA, and other trackers.

For automating user tasks around Premier League data, the most important endpoint families are: /api/v2/matches for fixtures and results, /api/v5/competitions/8/seasons/{season}/standings for league tables, /api/v1/competitions/8/seasons/{season}/teams and related team endpoints for club info and form, /api/v1/players/{id} and /api/v2/competitions/8/seasons/{season}/players/{id}/stats for player details and stats, and the /content/premierleague/* content APIs for surfacing associated articles, videos, promos and playlists. All of these are GET-only and stateless, making them well-suited for automation without needing to simulate complex auth flows.
